note: Mathematics round 3 (part B): geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, coordinate geometry, calculus, statistics, probability, vectors and longitude/latitude, with a test-marks frequency table and a daily-sales table as data passages.

passages.title: Marks of 40 students in a Mathematics test
passages.text:
The table shows the marks obtained by 40
students in a test marked out of 10.

Mark        3   4   5   6   7   8   9
Frequency   2   5   8  11   7   4   3

passages.title: Daily sales of bags of pure water at a kiosk
passages.text:
A kiosk owner recorded the number of bags
of pure water she sold each day for 30
days.

Bags sold      10  11  12  13  14  15
Number of days  3   6   9   7   3   2

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table of test marks above, the modal mark is
questions.explanation: The mode is the mark with the highest frequency: 6 (obtained by 11 students).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table of test marks above, the median mark is
questions.explanation: The 20th and 21st values (of 40) both lie in the mark-6 group (cumulative frequencies 2, 7, 15, 26), so the median is 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the mean mark, correct to one decimal place, is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the percentage of students who scored more than 6 marks is
questions.explanation: Students with 7, 8 or 9 marks: 7 + 4 + 3 = 14; 14/40 × 100 = 35%.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a pie chart is drawn from the table above, the angle of the sector representing students who scored 5 marks is
questions.explanation: 8 out of 40 students: 8/40 × 360° = 72°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the probability that a student chosen at random scored at most 4 marks is
questions.explanation: Marks of 3 or 4: 2 + 5 = 7 students out of 40.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the total number of bags sold in the 30 days is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the probability that on a day chosen at random she sold at least 13 bags is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the modal daily sale is
questions.explanation: 12 bags were sold on 9 days, more than any other number.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the median daily sale is
questions.explanation: The 15th and 16th days (cumulative frequencies 3, 9, 18) both fall in the 12-bag group, so the median is 12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Each bag in the table above sells at ₦300. The mean daily income from pure water, to the nearest naira, is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the table above, the range of the daily sales is
questions.explanation: Range = highest − lowest = 15 − 10 = 5 bags.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. The number of sides of the polygon is
questions.explanation: Exterior angles add to 360°, so 360/24 = 15 sides.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: PQ and RS are parallel lines and a transversal cuts PQ at A and RS at B. If the interior angle at A on one side of the transversal is 68°, the interior angle at B on the same side of the transversal is
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary: 180° − 68° = 112°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x°, (x + 20)°, (2x − 30)° and (3x + 20)°. The largest angle is
questions.explanation: Sum = 7x + 10 = 360, so x = 50; the angles are 50°, 70°, 70° and 170°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: O is the centre of a circle and A, B are points on it. If angle AOB = 80°, the angle ACB subtended by the chord AB at a point C on the minor arc is
questions.explanation: The angle at the major arc is 40° (half the angle at the centre); C on the minor arc is the opposite segment, so ACB = 180° − 40° = 140°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, angle P = (2x + 10)° and angle R = (3x − 20)°. The value of x is
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: 5x − 10 = 180, so x = 38.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point on the circumference. If angle CAB = 35°, then angle CBA is
questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is 90°, so angle CBA = 180° − 90° − 35° = 55°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From a point T outside a circle, a tangent TA and a secant TBC are drawn (B nearer to T). If TB = 4 cm and BC = 5 cm, the length of the tangent TA is
questions.explanation: TA² = TB × TC = 4 × 9 = 36, so TA = 6 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at X inside the circle. If AX = 6 cm, XB = 4 cm and CX = 3 cm, then XD is
questions.explanation: Intersecting chords: AX × XB = CX × XD, so 24 = 3 × XD and XD = 8 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A tangent PT touches a circle at T, and TQ is a chord such that angle PTQ = 50°. The angle in the alternate segment, i.e. the angle subtended by TQ at a point R on the major arc, is
questions.explanation: By the alternate segment theorem the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment: 50°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle PQR with AB = 6 cm, PQ = 9 cm and BC = 8 cm. The length of QR is
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides are in the ratio 9/6 = 1.5, so QR = 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A vertical pole 2 m high casts a shadow 3 m long at the same time that a tree casts a shadow 21 m long. The height of the tree is
questions.explanation: Similar triangles: height/shadow = 2/3, so the tree is 21 × 2/3 = 14 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In an isosceles triangle the vertical angle is 40°. Each base angle is
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal: (180° − 40°)/2 = 70°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The interior angles of a regular polygon total 1,800°. The polygon has

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which of the following statements about a rhombus is NOT always true?
questions.B: its diagonals bisect each other at right angles
questions.C: its diagonals are equal in length
questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides and perpendicular bisecting diagonals, but the diagonals are equal only when the rhombus is a square.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of a point that moves so that it is equidistant from two fixed points A and B is
questions.A: the bisector of the angle at A
questions.B: a circle with AB as diameter
questions.explanation: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from A as from B.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of a point in a plane that is always 5 cm from a fixed point O is
questions.A: a straight line 5 cm from O
questions.B: a circle of radius 5 cm with centre O
questions.explanation: Points at a fixed distance from a fixed point in a plane form a circle.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In triangle XYZ, the bisector of angle X meets YZ at W. If XY = 8 cm, XZ = 6 cm and YZ = 7 cm, the length of YW is
questions.explanation: The angle bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides, 8 : 6 = 4 : 3, so YW = 4/7 × 7 = 4 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The three angles of a triangle are (x + 15)°, (2x − 5)° and (3x + 20)°. The triangle is
questions.explanation: 6x + 30 = 180 gives x = 25; the angles are 40°, 45° and 95°, so one angle is obtuse.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two angles of a triangle are 48° and 67°. The exterior angle at the third vertex is
questions.explanation: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles: 48° + 67° = 115°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A chord of length 16 cm is 6 cm from the centre of a circle. The radius of the circle is
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: r² = 8² + 6² = 100, so r = 10 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rectangular room is 6 m long, 4.5 m wide and 3 m high. The area of its four walls is
questions.explanation: Perimeter × height = 2(6 + 4.5) × 3 = 21 × 3 = 63 m².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A circular flower bed of radius 3.5 m is surrounded by a path 1.5 m wide. The area of the path is (take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A cylindrical tin of radius 7 cm and height 15 cm is full of palm oil. The oil is poured into small bottles each holding 110 cm³. The number of bottles that can be filled completely is (take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius 7 cm is 25 cm. The angle of the sector is (take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 8 cm and 14 cm and an area of 77 cm². The perpendicular distance between the parallel sides is
questions.explanation: Area = ½(8 + 14)h = 11h = 77, so h = 7 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A solid cone has base radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. Its curved surface area is (take π = 3.14)
questions.explanation: Slant height = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm; curved surface = πrl = 3.14 × 6 × 10 = 188.4 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A solid metal cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 10 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm. The number of spheres formed is
questions.explanation: Cylinder volume = π × 36 × 10 = 360π; sphere volume = 4/3 π × 8 = 32π/3; 360π ÷ (32π/3) = 33.75, so 33 complete spheres.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rectangular tank 3 m by 2 m by 1.5 m is filled with water. The volume of water in litres is
questions.explanation: Volume = 3 × 2 × 1.5 = 9 m³ and 1 m³ = 1,000 litres, so 9,000 litres.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm is (take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Curved surface 2πr² = 308 cm² plus the flat circular face πr² = 154 cm²: total 462 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A square lawn of side 20 m has a circular pond of radius 7 m in the middle. The area of the grass is (take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Square area 400 m² minus pond area 22/7 × 49 = 154 m² leaves 246 m².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A frustum is made by cutting off the top of a cone of height 12 cm and base radius 6 cm by a plane parallel to the base and 4 cm from the top. The volume of the frustum is (take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of a rhombus whose diagonals are 12 cm and 16 cm is
questions.explanation: Area of a rhombus = ½ × product of diagonals = ½ × 12 × 16 = 96 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A conical tent has a base diameter of 14 m and a slant height of 10 m. The area of canvas needed for the curved surface is (take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Curved surface = πrl = 22/7 × 7 × 10 = 220 m².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A cube of side 4 cm and a cuboid 8 cm by 2 cm by x cm have the same volume. The value of x is
questions.explanation: Cube volume 4³ = 64 cm³; cuboid volume 8 × 2 × x = 16x; 16x = 64 gives x = 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The length of the diagonal of a cuboid 12 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The perimeter of a semicircular garden of diameter 28 m, including the straight edge, is (take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Half circumference = ½ × 22/7 × 28 = 44 m; add the diameter 28 m: 72 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A water tank in the shape of a cylinder has an internal radius of 1.4 m. When 6,160 litres of water are poured in, the depth of the water is (take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The volume of a pyramid on a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm is
questions.explanation: V = ⅓ × base area × height = ⅓ × 36 × 10 = 120 cm³.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the top of a building 30 m high, the angles of depression of two cars on the same side of the building are 30° and 60°. The distance between the cars is (take √3 = 1.73)
questions.explanation: Distances from the building: 30/tan 30° = 30√3 ≈ 51.9 m and 30/tan 60° = 10√3 ≈ 17.3 m; difference = 20√3 ≈ 34.6 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A boy stands 15 m from the foot of a flagpole and sees the top at an angle of elevation of 40°. If his eyes are 1.5 m above the ground, the height of the pole is (tan 40° = 0.84)
questions.explanation: Height above eye level = 15 × 0.84 = 12.6 m; total = 12.6 + 1.5 = 14.1 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If cos θ = −5/13 and 90° < θ < 180°, the value of tan θ is
questions.explanation: In the second quadrant sin θ = +12/13, so tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = (12/13)/(−5/13) = −12/5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of tan 225° is
questions.explanation: 225° is in the third quadrant where tan is positive: tan 225° = tan 45° = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A ship leaves port P and sails 24 km on a bearing of 060°, then 10 km on a bearing of 150°. Its distance from P is
questions.explanation: The two legs are at right angles (150° − 60° = 90°), so the distance is √(24² + 10²) = 26 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The bearing of village Y from village X is 245°. The bearing of X from Y is
questions.explanation: Back bearing = 245° − 180° = 065°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In triangle ABC, AB = 7 cm, BC = 8 cm and CA = 5 cm. The size of angle A is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of a triangle with sides 8 cm and 10 cm and an included angle of 30° is
questions.explanation: Area = ½ab sin C = ½ × 8 × 10 × sin 30° = 40 × 0.5 = 20 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solve 2 sin θ = 1 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
questions.explanation: sin θ = ½ at 30° and, in the second quadrant, at 180° − 30° = 150°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If sin θ = cos θ and θ is acute, then θ is
questions.explanation: sin θ = cos θ means tan θ = 1, so θ = 45°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Express sin 300° in terms of an acute angle.
questions.explanation: 300° = 360° − 60° is in the fourth quadrant where sine is negative: sin 300° = −sin 60°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90°, PQ = 5 cm and QR = 12 cm. The value of sin P + cos P is
questions.explanation: PR = 13 cm; sin P = 12/13 and cos P = 5/13, so the sum is 17/13.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A kite is flying at the end of a 50 m string which makes an angle of 55° with the horizontal ground. The height of the kite above the ground is (sin 55° = 0.819)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Simplify (1 − cos²θ)/sin θ cos θ.
questions.explanation: 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, so the expression is sin²θ/(sin θ cos θ) = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An aeroplane flies 100 km due north and then 100 km due east. Its bearing from the starting point is
questions.explanation: Equal legs north then east put it north-east of the start: bearing 045°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Town B is 12 km from town A on a bearing of 090°, and town C is 12 km from A on a bearing of 030°. The distance BC is
questions.explanation: Angle BAC = 60° and AB = AC, so triangle ABC is equilateral and BC = 12 km.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If tan x = 3/4 and x is acute, the value of (sin x − cos x)/(sin x + cos x) is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tree from a point 24 m from its base on level ground is 45°. When the observer walks towards the tree, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. The observer walked (take √3 = 1.73)
questions.explanation: Tree height = 24 m; new distance = 24/√3 ≈ 13.9 m; the observer walked 24 − 13.9 ≈ 10.1 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The gradient of the line 3x − 4y + 8 = 0 is
questions.explanation: Rearranging: 4y = 3x + 8, y = (3/4)x + 2, so the gradient is 3/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the line through (−1, 4) perpendicular to the line 2x − y = 5 is
questions.explanation: The given line has gradient 2, so the perpendicular has gradient −½: y − 4 = −½(x + 1), i.e. x + 2y = 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line joining (2, k) and (6, 9) has gradient 3/2. The value of k is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The distance between the points (−3, 2) and (5, −4) is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The point (3, −2) is the midpoint of the line joining A(1, 4) and B. The coordinates of B are
questions.explanation: (1 + x)/2 = 3 gives x = 5 and (4 + y)/2 = −2 gives y = −8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (2, 5) is
questions.explanation: Base 6 along the x-axis and height 5: ½ × 6 × 5 = 15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line y = 2x + c passes through the point (3, 1). The y-intercept of the line is
questions.explanation: 1 = 6 + c gives c = −5, and c is the y-intercept.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line joining (2, 3) and (6, −1) is
questions.explanation: Midpoint (4, 1); gradient of the segment = −1, so the bisector has gradient 1: y − 1 = x − 4, i.e. y = x − 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The lines 2x + 3y = 12 and 4x − y = 10 intersect at the point
questions.explanation: From the second, y = 4x − 10; substituting: 2x + 12x − 30 = 12, x = 3, y = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line through (4, −1) and (k, 5) is parallel to the line y = 3x + 2. The value of k is
questions.explanation: Gradient (5 + 1)/(k − 4) = 3 gives k − 4 = 2, so k = 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line 5x + 2y = 10 crosses the y-axis at the point
questions.explanation: On the y-axis x = 0, so 2y = 10 and y = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle between the line y = x − 4 and the positive x-axis is
questions.explanation: The gradient is 1 = tan 45°, so the line is inclined at 45°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the circle with centre (2, −3) and radius 4 is
questions.explanation: A circle with centre (a, b) and radius r is (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A straight line has x-intercept 4 and y-intercept −2. Its equation is
questions.explanation: Intercept form x/4 + y/(−2) = 1 gives x − 2y = 4 (check: (4, 0) and (0, −2) both satisfy it).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The perpendicular distance from the point (1, 2) to the line 3x + 4y − 21 = 0 is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Differentiate y = (2x + 1)(x − 3) with respect to x.
questions.explanation: Expand first: y = 2x² − 5x − 3, so dy/dx = 4x − 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The gradient of the curve y = 2x³ − 3x² + 1 at the point where x = 1 is
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 6x² − 6x; at x = 1 this is 6 − 6 = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The turning point of the curve y = x² − 4x + 7 is
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x − 4 = 0 gives x = 2 and y = 4 − 8 + 7 = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A rectangular pen is to be made against a wall using 40 m of fencing for the other three sides. The maximum area that can be enclosed is
questions.explanation: With width x and length 40 − 2x, A = 40x − 2x²; dA/dx = 40 − 4x = 0 at x = 10, so A = 10 × 20 = 200 m².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The distance s metres travelled by a car after t seconds is s = 3t² + 2t. Its velocity after 4 seconds is
questions.explanation: v = ds/dt = 6t + 2; at t = 4, v = 26 m/s.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A particle moves so that its velocity at time t is v = 3t² − 12t + 9. The particle is momentarily at rest when t equals

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Evaluate ∫₀² (3x² + 2x) dx.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find ∫ (4x³ − 6x + 2) dx.
questions.explanation: Integrate term by term: 4x⁴/4 − 6x²/2 + 2x + c = x⁴ − 3x² + 2x + c.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area enclosed between the curve y = 4 − x² and the x-axis is
questions.explanation: The curve meets the axis at x = ±2: ∫₋₂² (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3]₋₂² = (8 − 8/3) − (−8 + 8/3) = 32/3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The derivative of y = 1/x² with respect to x is
questions.explanation: y = x⁻², so dy/dx = −2x⁻³ = −2/x³.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The maximum value of the function y = 5 + 8x − 2x² is
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 8 − 4x = 0 at x = 2; y = 5 + 16 − 8 = 13 (a maximum since the x² coefficient is negative).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The rate at which the volume V of a sphere increases with its radius r, when r = 3 cm, is (V = 4/3 πr³)
questions.explanation: dV/dr = 4πr²; at r = 3 this is 4π × 9 = 36π.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If dy/dx = 6x − 4 and y = 5 when x = 1, the equation of the curve is
questions.explanation: y = 3x² − 4x + c; 5 = 3 − 4 + c gives c = 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The gradient of the tangent to the curve y = x³ − 5x at the point (2, −2) is
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² − 5; at x = 2 the gradient is 12 − 5 = 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upwards and its height h metres after t seconds is h = 40t − 5t². The stone reaches its greatest height after
questions.explanation: dh/dt = 40 − 10t = 0 when t = 4 s (the height is then 80 m).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Evaluate ∫₁³ (2x − 1) dx.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Differentiate y = (3x² + 1)⁴ with respect to x.
questions.explanation: Chain rule: 4(3x² + 1)³ × 6x = 24x(3x² + 1)³.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The derivative of y = sin 3x with respect to x is
questions.explanation: d/dx (sin kx) = k cos kx, so the derivative is 3 cos 3x.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean of 8 numbers is 15. If two of the numbers, 12 and 20, are removed, the mean of the remaining numbers is
questions.explanation: Total = 120; after removing 32 the total is 88 for 6 numbers: 88/6 = 14.67.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The ages of the members of a football team are 19, 21, 22, 22, 23, 24, 24, 24, 26, 27, 32. The median age is
questions.explanation: There are 11 values; the median is the 6th value in order, which is 24.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The numbers 5, 7, x, 9 and 11 have a mean of 8. The mode of the set is
questions.explanation: x = 40 − 32 = 8; the values 5, 7, 8, 9, 11 all occur once, so there is no mode.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The standard deviation of the numbers 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 is
questions.explanation: Mean = 7; squared deviations 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 sum to 40; variance = 40/5 = 8, so SD = √8 = 2√2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a pie chart of a family's monthly budget of ₦180,000, the sector for rent has an angle of 90°. The family spends on rent

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The scores of a student in five tests are 62, 70, 58, 74 and 66. The range of the scores is
questions.explanation: Range = highest − lowest = 74 − 58 = 16.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean of 20 numbers is 14. When one more number is added, the mean becomes 15. The number added is
questions.explanation: New total = 21 × 15 = 315; old total = 280; the number added is 35.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean deviation of the numbers 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 is
questions.explanation: Mean = 8; absolute deviations 4, 2, 0, 2, 4 sum to 12; 12/5 = 2.4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A class of 30 students has a mean mark of 60 and another class of 20 students has a mean mark of 70. The mean mark of the two classes combined is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a grouped frequency distribution the class 20–29 has a class boundary and class mark (mid-value) of
questions.explanation: Boundaries lie half a unit beyond the class limits (19.5 to 29.5); the class mark is (20 + 29)/2 = 24.5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The variance of a set of numbers is 25. The standard deviation is
questions.explanation: Standard deviation = √variance = √25 = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The histogram of a distribution has its tallest bar over the class 40–49. This tells us that the class 40–49 is the
questions.explanation: The tallest bar of a histogram (with equal class widths) marks the class with the highest frequency, the modal class.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a bar chart showing the number of goals scored by five teams, the bars have heights 12, 8, 15, 10 and 5. The mean number of goals per team is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A cumulative frequency curve (ogive) is used to estimate the
questions.explanation: Reading across from the middle of the cumulative frequency axis gives the median; the quarter marks give the quartiles.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The interquartile range of the numbers 3, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15, 18 is
questions.explanation: Lower quartile = median of 3, 6, 7, 8 → 6.5; upper quartile = median of 12, 14, 15, 18 → 14.5; IQR = 14.5 − 6.5 = 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The mean of the numbers 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 is 6. If each number is doubled, the new mean is
questions.explanation: Doubling every value doubles the mean: 12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The frequency table 1 (×3), 2 (×5), 3 (×7), 4 (×5) shows the number of children in 20 families. The mean number of children per family is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue and 3 white balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. The probability that both are blue is

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the scores is at least 10 is
questions.explanation: Sums of 10, 11 or 12 arise in 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 of the 36 outcomes: 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
